sections.heading: Not sure where to begin? Start here.
Eligibility, Services, and Support
sections.markdown:
**Eligibility**

The primary beneficiaries of the Family Member Assistance Program (FMEAP):

- Military spouses of active-duty service members.
- Dependent family member of active-duty service members.

**Getting Started**

- Connect with your local installation's FMEAP office. This will allow you to schedule an introductory meeting and learn more about the program.
- Attend FMEAP workshops. Many installations offer workshops or seminars on topics like resume building, interview techniques, and job search strategies.
- Register for the Military Spouse Employment Partnership. If you're interested in portable career opportunities, this program is essential. Registration can provide you with access to a network of employer partners.
- Explore MyCAA. If you're eligible and interested in pursuing further education, start the application process for the MyCAA scholarship.
- Stay engaged. Join the FMEAP mailing list or social media groups to stay updated on upcoming events, job fairs, and other opportunities.

**Available Services**

- Career Advising & Coaching
- Education, Entrepreneurial & Training Resources
- Individual Career Assessment & Planning
- Interviewing Skills
- Job Search Strategies
- Resume Assistance
- Salary Negotiations
- Volunteer & Skills Development
- Career Workshops

sections.heading: SpouseWorks
sections.markdown:
**Welcome, military spouses!**

The Office of Spouse Employment introduces **SpouseWorks** (formerly SECO). While the name has changed, the commitment to helping build meaningful careers remains the same.

SpouseWorks brings career and education support into one platform. Access:

- **Career Coaching & Advice:** Navigate every stage of your career journey.
- **Job Opportunities:** Find employers looking to hire military spouses.
- **Education & Funding:** Discover scholarships, fellowships, and training.

Connect at [SpouseWorks](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/). [Learn more about SpouseWorks](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/article/welcome-to-spouseworks)

sections.heading: SpouseWorks Scholarship
sections.markdown: Explore a workforce development program that provides up to $4,000 in financial assistance. [SpouseWorks Scholarship](https://mycaa.militaryonesource.mil/mycaa/)

sections.heading: Military Spouse Employer Partnership (MSEP)
sections.markdown: The Military Spouse Employer Partnership connects military spouses with hundreds of partner employers who have committed to recruit, hire, promote and retain military spouses. [MSEP](https://msepjobs.militaryonesource.mil/msep/)

sections.heading: Military Spouse Licensure Reimbursement (MSLR)
sections.markdown: If your career requires a professional license or certification, you may be eligible for up to $1,000 in reimbursement for licensure and certification costs resulting from relocations within the United States or from OCONUS to stateside. [MSLR](https://myseco.militaryonesource.mil/portal/article/licensure-reimbursement-pcs-moves)

sections.heading: Transferring Your Professional License
sections.markdown: Moving across the country – or around the world – can be a great adventure. Here's some help for making sure your licenses and certifications travel with you during your next move. [Transferring Your Professional License](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/education-employment/seco/transferring-your-professional-license-what-s-involved)

sections.heading: Spouse's Transition and Readiness Seminar (S.T.A.R.S)
sections.markdown: This workshop is designed to provide support and resources for military spouses as they navigate various aspects of transition, particularly during periods of relocation or when their service member is transitioning out of the military. Contact the FMEAP office for workshop availability in your area.
